title: Linear Algebra Approach for Directed Triad Counting and Enumeration
problem: Existing triangle counting algorithms are benchmarked on undirected graphs and are not suitable for identifying types of directed triangles in directed graphs. Current formulations fail to properly enumerate each type of directed triad.
motivation: Triangle and triad counting are commonly used in real-world applications on directed graphs, requiring specialized algorithms optimized for this setting.
method: The paper reformulates directed triad counting—identifying and counting specific patterns of directed connections between three nodes—as a linear algebra problem expressed through matrix operations. Using the FLAME methodology (a systematic framework for deriving algorithms from mathematical descriptions), they generate algorithms with mathematical proofs of correctness. By combining individual specialized algorithms (each designed to count one type of directed triad), they efficiently count all triads together, achieving faster results than previous graph-based approaches.
key_novelty: Using linear algebra and the FLAME methodology to systematically derive provably correct algorithms for directed triad counting.
contributions: Linear algebra formulation for directed triad counting
FLAME-based systematic derivation of provably correct counting and enumeration algorithms
Unified framework for counting individual triads and all-triads combined
Geometric mean speedup of 92.69x over NetworkX and 2.86x over GraphBLAS
primary_theme: graph algorithm optimization via linear algebra
